title: Public Restrooms Near Me: Toilets on the Map
description: Find nearby mapped toilets; public access, opening hours and availability are not verified.
summary_sentence: Results are limited to returned OpenStreetMap records and may omit closer or unmapped places. Confirm details with an authoritative local source.
quick_answer: The tool searches OpenStreetMap for mapped toilet records around a chosen location, then sorts returned records by straight-line distance. It requests at most 200 records and displays up to 100, so it cannot guarantee the closest result or a complete list. Data, access and opening status can be incomplete or outdated.

faq: Are these guaranteed open?
No — the map records existence, not hours. Seasonal closures, locked evenings and maintenance happen. Treat the pin as the best lead, and venues like stations and libraries as the reliable backups.
Why is my town's restroom missing?
It may be unrecorded, or recorded after the data snapshot. OpenStreetMap improves exactly when locals add the facilities they know.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
You can search for a place instead of using device location. The selected search centre is sent to OpenStreetMap-based services for the lookup.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Facility records vary by source — councils list theirs, businesses theirs; the open map is the merged, imperfect picture.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Device location is optional. The selected coordinates are sent to Overpass to search; consult the privacy page for provider and site details.
Accessible toilets specifically?
The workspace does not display or filter accessibility tags. Confirm access with the operator or an authoritative local source.
Baby-changing facilities?
The workspace does not show baby-changing details. Check with the venue.
Does it work in rural areas?
Village public toilets are recorded where communities map them — trailheads and car parks are the usual rural pins.
Can I add one I know?
Yes — OpenStreetMap editing is open to all, and a toilet you add helps every traveller after you. The highest use of local knowledge there is.
Pay-to-use toilets?
Fees are not shown. Confirm with the operator.
Night-time options?
Opening hours are not shown. Check with the operator before travelling.
